correctness.rationale: From G=1-exp(-A), A=exp(theta*x^vartheta-1/x), differentiating yields G'=x^(-2)(1+vartheta*theta*x^(vartheta+1))*A*exp(-A). For vartheta>0 and theta>0, A increases from 0 to infinity and G is a proper CDF. At theta=0 the mass on finite x is 1-e^(-1), leaving e^(-1) at infinity. At theta<0, A tends to 0 at infinity, G declines from its interior maximum and its derivative changes sign once at (-1/(vartheta*theta))^(1/(vartheta+1)); the formal PDF is negative after this point. Valid-theta hazard tends to 0 at x downarrow 0 and infinity at x infinity. Independently evaluated G(1)=0.12657698150688335, G(10)=0.000041078711471964624 and g(10)=-0.000040667089052803186 for vartheta=1, theta=-1, including threshold x=1. This is symbolic for all real theta; finite checks only illustrate.
